	<div class='heading'>
	<h1>Pantheons <a name='Nirrum's Encyclopedia of Varomar 2:Pantheons'></a></h1>
	</div>

	<div class='content'>
	<p>
Created Thursday 26 October 2023
</p>

<br>

<h3>Religious structures of civilizations around snarl<a id="religious-structures-of-civilizations-around-snarl" class="h_anchor"></a></h3>

<br>

<h4>The Manarahi<a id="the-manarahi" class="h_anchor"></a></h4>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
All major groups of the Manarahi consider the gods to be citizens and people. They are powerful beings but they have both rights and duties that supercede their position. Gods must do work to be allowed to participate in Manarahi society and not be a detriment. The more in line with society's beliefs, the more involved directly in Manarahi civilization they are. Only two gods hold common temples among the Manarahi, and they are Charity and Knowledge. 
</div>
</p>

<br>

<h4>Konians<a id="konians" class="h_anchor"></a></h4>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Konia's gods are venerated as kings above kings, leaders above leaders. It is viewed that it is impossible for a god to not earn their position and thus they have rights to it, but it is wise to only venerate the ones that benefit your lord, for those are the ones that benefit you. 
</div>
</p>

<br>

<h4>Danzuishan<a id="danzuishan" class="h_anchor"></a></h4>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
The Gods exceed anything mortals can do to the Danzuishanese people. Ask blessings and boons all you want from them but they only reward their most faithful. Gods also embody what one <i>should be</i>.
</div>
</p>

<br>

<h4>Skalmirthon<a id="skalmirthon" class="h_anchor"></a></h4>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Gods among the dwarves are ritual pillars that they organise their meditations around. A dwarf should venerate the god that provides what challenges them the most, rather than the ones that already favour them. There is a divide in dwarven cosmogony between a god and their malevolent counterpart, which usually gets a new name. Gods themselves have commented on this shift in perspective as weird but plausible, as a way to differentiate what the god does control and what happens within the god's domain outside of its control.<br>
The drow of Skalmirthon and Cermina are emphatically antitheist, and special rites might be observed to prevent them from being drawn into the hells on death, instead powering a great, secret elven project in the feywild
</div>
</p>

<h4>Kara'ite<a id="karaite" class="h_anchor"></a></h4>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Gods are a mark or a guiding spirit in Kara'ite, as so very little obfuscates holiness as capitalism. Churches are places for the stupid to lose money and for the occasional gang to make a home. Those who are selected by gods sometimes rise up, on occasion literally, from the depths of the pit to escape kara'ite
</div>
</p>

<br>

<h4>Shaat'guun<a id="shaatguun" class="h_anchor"></a></h4>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
The hobgoblins feel alienated by most gods and conquered by others, thus they serve
</div>
</p>

<br>
<br>
<br>
<br>

<h3>The Wandering Housed Gods<a id="the-wandering-housed-gods" class="h_anchor"></a></h3>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
The housed or wandering gods are deities who are understood and welcomed within most societies in some capacity. They are named for being both alien to this world (having come from others), and having been able to maintain temples and stable worship, offerings, sacrifice, or following, varying between each. 
</div>
</p>

<br>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Maianosé
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
God of Agriculture, domain of suns, food, and small comforts. Protects against disease, the pain of age, hunger, drought and plague. Generally Masculine. Humanoid
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Hurikilo
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
Goddess of Civilization, Domain of buildings, Civil engineering, Infrastructure, and Politics. Protects against corruption, building collapse, bad policy decisions, and bureaucracy. Generally Feminine. Humanoid
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Taylo
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
God of Knowledge, domain of Machines, Learning, Language, and Science. Protects against ignorance. Largely genderless. Arachnoid
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Awhoonooriamoo
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
God of Oceans, Domain of large bodies of water. Protects against Large bodies of Water, and the things in them. Kinda. Generally Masculine. Cetaceoid
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Mehinolikoneratemmenatonorigonae
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
God of Dragons, Domain of ambitions, treasure, personal power. Protects against theives, curses. Generally Feminine. Draconid
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Eelu
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
God of Wilds, domains of uncivilised lands, predators, and escape. Protects against predators and being found. Ambiguous. Depicted as various animals, depending on purpose.
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Sha
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
Goddess of Death, domain of winter, the grave, night, cold ash, and sleep. Protects against insomnia, gross violations of the soul and person, trauma, and interruptions.  Generally Feminine. Avian.
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Karak'dal
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
God of War, Domain of storms, waves, battle, necessity, and heroism. Protects against stagnation, premature ends, slipping hazards, unfinished goals. Most frequently masculine. Canid.
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
 Otokadon 
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
God of Beauty, Domain of craft, art, aesthetic, and skill. Protects against dullness, a lack of inspiration, Boredom, and stunted growth. Most frequently feminine, form varies wildly.
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Uumo
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
God-thing of the worms. Domain of Life, Evolution, Peace, Fertility, and Theophany. Protects against irrelevance, loneliness, infertility, and the death of rare family. A bloated and lazy creature, of indeterminate gender.
</div>
</p>

<br>

<h3>The Unhoused Gods<a id="the-unhoused-gods" class="h_anchor"></a></h3>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
The Unhoused Gods are gods who could not establish a temple but still exist in the world. Often they are rejected by a culture as a whole but supported by a few supplicants.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Sacrifice, Disease, Magic, 
</div>
</p>
